headline: Oil Prices Plunge 7% on U.S.-Iran Diplomacy Signals
summary: Oil prices dropped nearly 7% as Washington and Tehran signaled a willingness for diplomacy, reducing the war premium. Brent fell to $105.60 per barrel and WTI declined to $96.92.
why: Crude oil is a vital global commodity input affecting energy costs, inflation measures, and the operating expenses of transportation and manufacturing sectors worldwide.

impacts.name: Brent Crude
impacts.why: Directly reported price decline of Brent crude due to eased geopolitical tensions.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

impacts.name: WTI Crude
impacts.why: WTI prices fell alongside Brent as diplomatic signals reduced the geopolitical risk premium.

why_moved: Diplomatic signals between the U.S. and Iran lowered perceived risks of supply disruptions, prompting an immediate unwinding of the war premium built into crude futures.
